jobs.title: Senior Technical Program Manager, Partner Trip Platform
jobs.description:
Waymo is an autonomous driving technology company with the mission to be the world's most trusted driver. Since its start as the Google Self-Driving Car Project in 2009, Waymo has focused on building the Waymo Driver—The World's Most Experienced Driver™—to improve access to mobility while saving thousands of lives now lost to traffic crashes. The Waymo Driver powers Waymo’s fully autonomous ride-hail service and can also be applied to a range of vehicle platforms and product use cases. The Waymo Driver has provided over ten million rider-only trips, enabled by its experience autonomously driving over 100 million miles on public roads and tens of billions in simulation across 15+ U.S. states.

Waymo’s Technical Program Managers and Program Managers are accountable for Waymo’s roadmap execution by providing thoughtful cross-functional planning, clarity, and proactive risk management. In the face of complex technical and operational challenges with no established playbooks to follow, we act with thoughtful urgency, driving conversations, discussions, and outcomes. Our team partners closely with every function of Waymo to structure, own and drive work towards real-world deployments of the Waymo Driver across platforms and geographies.

You Will

Lead cross-functional technical programs to integrate Waymo's autonomous service with third-party platforms.
Own the technical delivery of external integrations end-to-end, from creating the cross-functional execution plan to defining the process for ensuring continued quality post-launch.
Serve as the primary execution counterpart for external teams, translating an ambiguous set of work into clearly defined deliverables, owners, and schedule.
Drive technical trade-off decisions across scope, schedule, scalability, and user experience.
Proactively identify, prioritize, and mitigate risks and dependencies across multiple concurrent partner programs, and represent them to executive leadership.
Build the scalable frameworks, processes, and tooling that let Waymo onboard and operate many partner integrations without a linear increase in effort.

You Have

7+ years of experience leading highly complex, cross-functional technical programs with a holistic understanding of business-wide functions (e.g. Product, Engineering, Business Development, Operations).
A track record of shipping consumer-facing software products and features, with demonstrated ownership of the execution from kickoff through launch and post-launch operations.
Experience running programs where critical dependencies sit with teams outside your direct influence, and a track record of getting them to deliver.
Strong technical depth: you can read a system design, hold your own in architecture and API discussions with engineers, and tease out the scope, schedule, and risk implications of each option to drive the decision.
Deep care for the end user, with the ability to keep rider experience and quality at the center of technically complex, multi-party programs.
Exceptional communication and leadership skills, with demonstrated ability to align diverse internal teams and external partners and influence executive stakeholders.

We Prefer

Experience with external-facing integrations, platform APIs, or B2B2C products where another company's engineering team was a critical dependency.
Experience in rideshare, mobility, delivery, two-sided marketplaces, or other products where software coordinates physical operations in real time.
Experience launching products or integrations in multiple geographies, including navigating localization, payments, and regulatory requirements.
Familiarity with defining quality gates, testing plans, SLAs, and launch readiness processes for systems shared with external teams.

Travel Requirements

Occasional travel for partner working sessions or market launches

The expected base salary range for this full-time position across US locations is listed below. Actual starting pay will be based on job-related factors, including exact work location, experience, relevant training and education, and skill level. Your recruiter can share more about the specific salary range for the role location or, if the role can be performed remote, the specific salary range for your preferred location, during the hiring process.

Waymo employees are also eligible to participate in Waymo’s discretionary annual bonus program, equity incentive plan, and generous Company benefits program, subject to eligibility requirements.

Salary Range

$230,000—$284,000 USD

jobs.title: Technical Program Manager - Pharmacy Care
jobs.description:
The Technical Program Manager, Pharmacy Care owns the delivery of our largest and most complex pharmacy platform programs. This is a hands-on technical delivery role for someone who can hold a multi-party, multi-phase implementation together: integration dependencies across organizations, contractual milestones with defined acceptance criteria, regulated launch requirements, and a phased rollout that moves from a controlled pilot all the way through government-program populations.

You will be the connective tissue between Product, Engineering, Design, Solutions, Data, Security, Compliance, Client Services, Service Delivery, and external partners. The work is equal parts technical fluency and program discipline . Y ou need to be able to read an API specification, run the integration conversation on your own, and then convert what you heard into a plan, a dependency, or an escalation. If a date is going to move, you know first and you say so early.

This program delivers a pharmacy-first digital member experience: medic ine cabinet , claims and prior-authorization visibility, real-time price transparency, benefit and accumulator presentment, digital ID cards, document access, member notifications, an AI care assistant, and the partner integrations that power all of it.

What you'll do

Own the program end to end

Own delivery of a multi-phase, enterprise-scale platform implementation from mobilization and discovery through pilot, staged client rollout, and transition to ongoing operations.
Structure the program into workstreams with clear owners, milestones, and exit criteria.
Build and maintain the integrated program plan: scope, milestones, critical path, dependencies, acceptance criteria, and readiness gates across every workstream.
Sequence phased rollout waves : internal pilot, shared pilot clients, standard commercial rollout, strategic accounts, and regulated and government-program populations
Drive milestone attainment where milestones carry contractual acceptance criteria and commercial consequence . Know exactly what must be true for each gate to close.

Drive the technical integration

Coordinate delivery across the full integration surface: eligibility, identity and authentication, claims history, accumulators, formulary and medication data, real-time pricing, prior-authorization status and intake, document retrieval, event and webhook interfaces, notifications, and federated SSO connections.
Work with Engineering and Architecture on integration design, data mapping, identifier reconciliation across systems, environment strategy, and interface specifications covering authentication, schemas, idempotency, error handling, monitoring, and reconciliation.
Hold the line on data quality and interface readiness , real-time versus batch trade-offs, validation rigor, and what happens when bad data moves downstream fast.
Manage partner-side technical dependencies rigorously: API documentation and sandbox access, file specifications and cadence, test data and credentials, environment provisioning, technical SMEs, and approvals. Track them, age them, and escalate with evidence before they become schedule impacts.

Run governance and quality

Establish and run program governance: meeting cadence, status reporting, RAID log, decision records, RASCI ownership across organizations, and executive-level reporting that tells the truth concisely.
Own scope discipline. Distinguish clarification from expansion, route genuine change through a documented change-control process and protect the committed timeline.
Partner with QA and Engineering to maintain a live quality and release-readiness view : test coverage and execution, defect counts by severity and trend, automation and regression status, environment and test-data blockers, and an honest Green/Yellow/Red call.
Produce release readiness summaries ahead of each major milestone: included and deferred scope, test and UAT completion, open defects and mitigations, security, privacy, performance and accessibility results, residual risk, and a clear Go / Go-with-conditions / No-Go recommendation.
Run post-production validation after each go-live — smoke checks, incident and defect capture, corrective actions, and follow-through.

Carry the regulated-delivery load

Coordinate security and privacy readiness: penetration testing and vulnerability assessment evidence, HIPAA security and privacy review, remediation plans for critical and high findings, compensating controls, and formal sign-off gates.
Drive accessibility conformance, including testing evidence, remediation, and an exceptions process.
Manage government-program readiness : regulatory requirement schedules, program-specific accumulator presentment, required member documents, regulatory data-format transitions, and the phased commitments and approvals that go with them.
Ensure AI-enabled member functionality ships within approved governance: guardrails, escalation pathways, PHI handling, retention, auditability, and change-approval requirements.

Build the operating model

Coordinate a distributed delivery team spanning product, design, engineering in the US and Europe, solutions, data and analytics, service delivery, and go-to-market.
Stand up operational readiness ahead of scale: implementation playbooks, configuration and administrative tooling, documentation, train-the-trainer enablement, support and escalation model, and contact-center integration.
Define the reporting and analytics requirements the program is measured by : engagement and funnel data, feature utilization , communication delivery, and the extract or sync mechanics that deliver it.
Define and track program health metrics: milestone attainment, dependency aging, defect burndown, integration readiness, launch readiness, and post-launch stability.
Transition the program cleanly into ongoing governance and continuous delivery rather than leaving an implementation that nobody owns.

What we're looking for

Required

Bachelor's degree required ; a technical discipline or an advanced degree is a plus.
7+ years in technical program or project management, including ownership of enterprise-scale integration programs in healthcare or another regulated industry.
Demonstrated experience leading multi-party programs with external partners , delivered against defined milestones, dependencies, and acceptance criteria.
T echnical fluency. REST APIs, authentication and federated identity (SSO, SAML, OIDC), batch file interfaces, event and webhook architectures, data mapping, and schema validation. You can read a specification, run the technical conversation yourself, and hold both engineers and partners to what was agreed .
Hands-on experience with healthcare data domains : eligibility, claims, benefit accumulators, formulary and medication data, and prior authorization.
Experience delivering in a regulated environmen t: HIPAA and PHI handling, security revie w , privacy requirements, and accessibility obligations.
Proven ownership of quality and release readiness : test strategy, UAT coordination, defect triage, and the judgment to make a defensible go/no-go call.
Exceptional written communication. This role produces the artifacts other people make decisions from : plans, status, readiness summaries, escalations. They must be clear, accurate , and to the point .
Rigorous on scope and change control , and comfortable saying no with a reason and a path.
Comfortable in a fast-moving, evolving organization ; a ble to replan without losing the thread.

Preferred

Pharmacy or pharmacy benefits ecosystem experience : pharmacy claims, formulary, pricing and adjudication concepts, specialty and mail-order fulfillment, or related integrations.
Medicare or other government-program delivery experience, including CMS requirements, program-specific accumulator stages, required member communications, and regulatory format transitions.
Experience with multi-tenant platform delivery and client-by-client configuration at scale.

Who we are

Transcarent is the One Place for Health and Careᵀᴹ, bringing medical, pharmacy, and point solutions together with the WayFinding ᵀᴹ experience, the first and only generative AI-powered health and care platform for health consumers.

Our WayFinding experience, paired with transparent and consumer-driven pharmacy care, 2nd.MD expert medical opinions, and virtual primary care, works seamlessly with comprehensive Care Experiences — Cancer Care, Surgery Care, and Weight Health — to support people with all of their health needs, simple or serious. McKinstry is innovating the waste and climate harm out of the built environment and creating lasting impact. Together, we’re building a thriving planet.

The Opportunity with McKinstry

McKinstry is looking for a Senior Program Manager, Standardization
to join our Offsite Manufacturing division in Seattle, WA
. The Senior Program Manager – Standardization leads the development, release, and adoption of the business processes that run the business unit and leads execution of the department's technology and business process improvement initiatives. The role's current top priority is leading implementation of Acumatica, the business unit's ERP system — building and maintaining the implementation schedule, providing status updates, and documenting the business process decisions made along the way — with the same playbook applied to future technology and process initiatives. Beyond named initiatives, the role focuses on business unit processes, especially those that cross functional boundaries where commercial, engineering, supply chain, operations, quality, project management, and finance must hand off work to one another. This role shapes how the business executes and drives development of documented, governed, repeatable standard work. Additional responsibilities may include:

Business Process Leadership

Own the process roadmap for the business unit, sequencing standardization work against live production commitments, growth targets, and customer program milestones.
Maintain the business unit’s process architecture: what processes exist, who owns each, how they connect, and where the gaps are.
Translate business objectives into standardization objectives and measures with leadership and report progress regularly.
Advise leaders on where standardization creates leverage and where flexibility should be intentionally preserved.
Initiative and Implementation Management
Lead the implementation of Acumatica (ERP), including building and maintaining the implementation schedule and providing regular status updates.
Apply the same implementation approach — schedule ownership, decision documentation, stakeholder alignment — to future technology and process improvement initiatives.
Organize and execute department business process improvement initiatives from scoping through completion.
Draft and propose OKRs for initiatives or execute against and report progress on OKRs set by leadership, depending on the initiative.
Source, select, and manage contractors and consultants supporting initiatives, owning scope, schedule, and budget for those engagements.

Cross-Functional Process Integration

Lead standardization of processes that span multiple functions, including order intake and contract-to-production handoff, engineering release and change control, procurement and long-lead material planning, production scheduling and capacity, quality and nonconformance, shipping and field integration, and warranty and closeout.
Define the inputs, outputs, ownership, and acceptance criteria at each functional handoff so work does not stall or degrade in the gaps between teams.
Resolve conflicting or duplicative practice between functions, escalating to leadership where process ownership is genuinely contested.
Embed processes into the systems of record – ERP, document control, quality management, and reporting – so process is reinforced by tooling rather than carried by individual experience.
Reconcile customer-specific commercial requirements with internal standard work so program obligations are met without one-off process.

Process Development and Release

Coordinate cross-functional teams through a standard development process to produce released, version-controlled deliverables.
Write and review policies, procedures, work instructions, and supporting documentation — including documenting the business process decisions made during initiative implementations — with process owners and subject matter experts.
Establish document control, revision, and approval conventions so processes are governed.

Change Management, Training, and Adoption

Develop implementation plans supporting communication, training, and sustained adoption of process deliverables.
Train project teams and operational leaders on the standard development process.
Communicate initiatives in small and large group settings, developing materials calibrated to mixed executive, commercial, engineering, operations, and craft audiences.

Team Leadership and Performance

Build process capability inside functional teams so ownership sits with the business, not solely with the program.
Track measures of process health: adoption and conformance, cycle time, rework and escape rates, audit findings, and other metrics as appropriate.
Route lessons learned back into the applicable processes.
No direct reports Day 1; may take on direct personnel management responsibility as the team grows.

Other duties as assigned.

What You Need To Succeed At McKinstry

Bachelor’s Degree required (industrial, mechanical, or manufacturing engineering, operations management, or supply chain preferred).
Minimum eight (8) years of team and/or project management experience required.
Demonstrated experience developing and deploying business process, standard work, or a quality management system across multiple functions in a manufacturing, industrialized construction, or offsite fabrication environment required.
Demonstrated ability to collaborate with and influence people at all levels across the organization required.
Excellent facilitation skills and the ability to lead diverse, cross-functional project teams required.
Ability to operate effectively in a high-growth environment where process and governance are authored in parallel with live production commitments.
Demonstrated experience managing scope, schedule, and budget for contractor or consulting engagements required.
Strongly Preferred: technical writing; engineer-to-order or high-mix production experience; ERP implementation experience (Acumatica preferred),, PLM, or document control systems; PMI certification; ISO 9001 or equivalent quality management system; LEAN Construction.

When it comes to the basics, we have you covered:

Competitive pay
401(k) with employer match and profit-sharing plan
Paid time off and holidays
Comprehensive medical, prescription, dental, and vision with low or zero deductible options and low out of pocket maximums

WHSmith North America is looking for an experienced Senior IT Project Manager to lead the delivery of technology projects across our North American retail estate.

The successful candidate will understand what it takes to open, change, refresh and close stores and will be comfortable coordinating multiple technology suppliers, internal IT teams, retail operations and other business stakeholders.
The role will be based in Las Vegas but will support projects across North America, including stores within airports and other travel locations.

Lead IT projects from initial requirements and planning through implementation, cutover, handover and closure.
Manage technology delivery for new store openings, store refurbishments, relocations and store closures.
Develop and maintain project plans, budgets, RAID logs, dependencies, milestones and delivery reporting.
Coordinate internal IT teams, business stakeholders, third-party technology vendors, contractors and service providers.
Own the technology readiness plan for store openings and ensure all technology is installed, configured, tested and operational before opening.
Manage store decommissioning, including removal or redeployment of technology assets, service termination and secure disposal where required.
Manage multiple concurrent projects across geographically dispersed locations.
Work closely with Retail Operations, Store Development, Construction, Finance, Loss Prevention and other functions to coordinate store delivery.
Manage technology cutovers and provide clear go/no-go criteria for store launches.
Ensure appropriate operational handover to support teams following implementation.
Identify project risks and issues early and drive them through to resolution.
Manage third-party suppliers against agreed deliverables, dates and service expectations.
Ensure project documentation, technical standards and governance requirements are followed.
Provide clear project status reporting to senior IT and business stakeholders.
Continually improve the standard approach, templates and processes used for retail technology deployments.

Point of Sale (POS)
Payment terminals and payment services
Store LAN, WAN and Wi-Fi
Internet and telecommunications circuits
Back-office systems
PCs, tablets and mobile devices
Printers and peripheral devices
Handheld scanners and inventory devices
Stock and inventory systems
Digital signage

Store servers and edge technology where applicable
Device configuration and deployment
Structured cabling
Technology asset management
Remote support and store support models

Design → Procurement → Connectivity → Installation → Configuration → Testing → Cutover → Opening → Hypercare → Handover

They should understand issues such as circuit lead times, equipment delivery, site access, construction dependencies, POS configuration, payment testing, stock-system readiness and opening-day support.

Asset identification and recovery
Equipment redeployment
Network and telecom service termination
POS and payment device removal
Data/security considerations
Supplier coordination
Asset disposal
Updating configuration and asset-management records

Minimum 5 years’ experience delivering IT projects.

Experience managing multiple projects concurrently.
Experience managing third-party technology vendors.

Multi-site retail
Hospitality
High-volume retail environments
POS replacement programmes
Network/Wi-Fi deployments
Payment technology

Large-scale store rollout programmes

Project planning and scheduling
Budget management
RAID management
Vendor management
Stakeholder management
Change control
Dependency management
Project governance
Executive reporting
Cutover planning
Operational readiness
Lessons learned and continuous improvement

jobs.description:
Position Details:

Job Title: Project Manager

Location: Minneapolis, MN 55441

Duration: 12+ Month Contract on W2 (no C2C or 1099)

Duties:

The Project Manager has the responsibility of managing the details of the assigned project plans (i.e., project planning and management, configuration planning and execution, testing and validation, and go live planning and support) under the leadership and governance of the Project Management Office (PMO). This role will use strong project, task, and resource management experiences and skills to assist the organization in achieving its goals of executing projects on time, on budget, and within scope. In performing these responsibilities, this position will work closely with business leaders and project leaders to assess and track the various activities and resources required in project management.
The position will utilize various project management solutions to develop, monitor, and communicate to the head of the PMO and business leaders. This role will also provide a framework for project leaders to use in initializing new projects within the PMO structure and processes.
The Project Manager will lead and perform all phases of project management activities including scope management, requirements definition and analysis, technical development, testing, validation, communication management, risk management, progress reporting, and budget and resource management.
The Project Manager will provide training is as appropriate to project participants and business partners regarding the use of various tools utilized and required by the PMO.
The position carries responsibility for ensuring that project plans and execution support client strategic plans, activities, and objectives while maintaining the highest level of ethics and compliance.

Principal Duties and Responsibilities:

Lead and provide project management capability for implementation of small to large scale solutions through the development and maintenance of detailed project plans, the organization of project implementation teams, the establishment of and adherence to project budget management, and the effective and timely execution of projects.
Develop and maintain the Master Project Plan and Schedule.
Responsible for the achievement of project milestones and metrics. Responsible for ensuring governance and compliance of the PMO methodology and related objectives.
Drive excellence of portfolio management by incorporating and supporting processes and tools that are used to identify, prioritize, and select opportunities/projects for optimal portfolio value and strategic alignment.
Collect and analyze the performance of the projects by collecting data for key metrics, including performance to budget, and regularly reporting out performance via dashboards and other appropriate, efficient, and progressive methods.
Lead and ensure the documentation and tracking of project reviews.
Ensure proactive mitigation and escalation of concerns, risks, issues, project dependencies, scope change, and project conflicts.
Assist and coordinate change management activities.
Provide consulting services and project management support to other functions and initiatives globally.
Collaborate cross-functionally with Operations, Quality, Finance, IT, Human Resources, etc. to ensure effective business case development, establishment of and adherence to project budget, tracking of relevant project metrics, achievement of expected outcomes, adherence to quality assurance and regulatory compliance requirements, creation of technical documentation, execution of testing activities, and the design and management of security requirements both technological and otherwise.
Act as a change agent for continuous improvement efforts that cross clients, sites, and processes.
Develop best practices and tools for project execution and management.

Skills
:
Ability to engage peers and subordinates at all locations and levels to work together for the most efficient and optimized use of all resources.
Excellent written, presentation, and communication skills with the ability to articulate complex ideas and strategies clearly and persuasively to diverse audiences at various organizational levels.
Ability to work across regions, divisions, and functions to influence change across the organization and unleash full potential as a company and as individuals.
Ability to engage internal business partners and team members at all levels of the organization and effectively present ideas and concepts to executive leaders.
Ability to establish relationships quickly with a broad range of constituents. Must possess a collaborative style to work effectively throughout the organization. Able to work with people in such a manner as to build high morale and group commitment to goals and objectives.
Cross-cultural negotiations and communications skills are essential.
Able to take action in solving problems and making decisions while exhibiting judgment and a realistic understanding of issues, able to use reason, even when dealing with emotional topics.
Personal/professional integrity with the ability to preserve confidentiality.
Extensive knowledge of manufacturing operations and facilities.
Knowledge of the medical technology industry and competitive landscape strongly preferred.

Education:

Bachelor's Degree (master's degree, MBA preferred) in Manufacturing, Engineering, Industrial Psychology, Industrial Engineering, or a related field.
Minimum four years of related experience required.
Commensurate combination of education and experience may be considered.
Significant manufacturing operations experience required.
Project management certification (such as PMP) or formal training strongly preferred.
Six Sigma or Lean Sigma certification strongly preferred.
Experience leading multiple cross-functional and inter-site project teams within operations with results-oriented performance.
Proficient with project management software.
Proficient in MS Office applications.
Experience in medical device regulatory environment or another regulatory environment preferred.

jobs.description:
Build the future, spark innovation and align your career with purpose.

McKinstry is innovating the waste and climate harm out of the built environment and creating lasting impact. Together, we’re building a thriving planet.

Buildings are a leading contributor to the climate crisis, generating nearly 40% of total global energy-related carbon emissions. We’re making a lasting impact on our industry and within our communities by addressing the climate, affordability and equity crises through:

renewables and energy services
engineering and design
construction and facility services

To get where we’re going, we need big thinkers, problem solvers and collaborative mindsets. Does that sound like you?

The Opportunity with McKinstry

We are adding a  Senior Project Manager to
our nationally growing Electrical INW division in Spokane, WA
. In this role, you will assume higher complexity projects, client relationships, and revenue oversight and may direct more than one Project Manager with oversight of their projects. Additionally, some responsibilities you will have include:

Project Management

Leads projects from initiation to closeout. 
Develops and manages project plans, schedules, and scopes of work.
Oversees, scheduling and coordination of internal and external resources for project completion.
Communicates with clients and project resources (subcontractors and vendors).
Documents discussions, outcomes, and decisions
Supports Request for Proposal (RFP) process.
Researches and evaluates new products and vendors.
Processes or oversees review log and distributes submittals.
Obtains detailed knowledge of contract, drawings and specifications for project(s).
Maintains or oversees the cost issue logs.
Upholds and communicates McKinstry safety standards.
Ensures safety compliance of subcontractors and all on-site personnel.
Defines individual project responsibilities and accountabilities. 
Coordinates implementation handoffs between internal departments.
Mitigates and reports on risk on behalf of the company.
Delivers accurate and timely business reports. 
Manages and coordinates procurement activities for Subcontracts and Purchase Orders.
Oversees Job Start and Project Closeout materials. 
Assesses, defines and documents agreements from customers regarding project requirements. 
Manages pre-construction process with the field foremen and Business Manager.
Assess site safety and implements actions to prevent injury to property and personnel.
Ensures safety compliance of subcontractors and all on-site personnel. 

Project Controls 

Assumes financial responsibility for project including accurate, timely and relevant reporting to stakeholders.
Facilitates invoice payment to subcontractors and suppliers.
Reviews substantiation of subcontractor billing.
Responsible for preparation of monthly project accounting review.
Monitors, controls, and reports on the financial performance of projects.
Draft or oversee subcontracts and purchase agreements.
Assist with client billings.
Generates preliminary assessments, technical solutions, fee proposals, presentations, studies, and general support.
Maintains positive working relationships with building owners, contractors, consultants, vendors and partners.
Respond to stakeholder inquiries.
Delivers accurate and timely data to support project forecasts. 

Communicate

Serve as primary point of contact with customer.
Inform internal and external customers of new offerings and upgrades.
Facilitate communication internally between project team and other departments.
Make presentations to a variety of audiences; act as subject matter expert.
Identify, qualify and funnel potential new service opportunities to Business Development team.
Directs customer requests for product functionality enhancements to the appropriate people. 

Team Management

Recruits, coaches, and mentors project team members.
Develop project staffing plans to include labor and subcontractors.
Responsible for the forecasting of project management labor requirements.
Act as steward of McKinstry culture; communicate and influence policies and procedures. 

Other duties as assigned.

Must have demonstrated proficiency for all the responsibilities of a Project Manager.
BA/BS degree in Construction Management, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Architecture, Facilities Management or equivalent work experience required.

Experience with working for a General Contractor or Major Mechanical Subcontractor required.

Knowledge of construction financial programs and software.
Basic estimating skills preferred.
Knowledge of the basics of labor relations including union contract requirements, and hiring practices preferred.

Competitive pay

Comprehensive medical, prescription, dental, and vision with low or zero deductible options and low out of pocket maximums

Carepod is a premium humidifier brand originally designed in Korea, known for our stainless steel water tanks, filter-free system, and elevated design. We operate across the U.S., Canada, and Australia, with strong seasonal performance in Q4 and continued growth year over year.
As we enter our next stage of growth, we are looking for a results-driven Project Manager
to help streamline operations, improve internal processes, and implement scalable solutions across our teams.

Role Overview

We are looking for a highly organized and proactive Project Manager who can turn operational challenges into practical, measurable improvements.

This role will focus primarily on process optimization, workflow automation, and cross-functional project execution
, working closely with our AI & Automation Specialists and department leaders.

You will own projects from planning through imple mentation, ensuring solutions are delivered on time, adopted by teams, and generate meaningful improvements in efficiency.

Reporting to the Senior Project Manager, you will also support larger business initiatives, product launches, and cross-departmental projects as needed.

Key Responsibilities

⚙️ Process Improvement & Optimization

Identify operational inefficiencies, workflow bottlenecks, and opportunities for improvement across departments.
Map existing processes and develop more efficient, scalable workflows.
Lead process improvement initiatives from planning through implementation.
Define project objectives, timelines, deliverables, and measurable success metrics.
Evaluate results and continuously identify opportunities to improve operational performance.

🤖 Automation & Systems Implementation

Partner with AI & Automation Specialists to identify and prioritize automation opportunities.
Translate business needs into clear project requirements and implementation plans.
Coordinate automation development, testing, and rollout across teams.
Ensure new systems and workflows are properly implemented, documented, and adopted.
Track automation outcomes, including time savings, error reduction, and operational efficiency.

📊 Project Management & Execution

Manage multiple projects simultaneously, ensuring clear ownership, priorities, and deadlines.
Coordinate stakeholders across Marketing, Operations, Customer Support, HR, and other departments.
Monitor project progress, identify risks, and proactively resolve roadblocks.
Maintain project plans, timelines, and status updates using project management tools.
Support the Senior Project Manager on strategic initiatives, launches, and cross-functional projects.

📝 SOPs & Change Management

Develop and maintain clear, practical Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).
Work with department owners to standardize processes and improve consistency.
Coordinate training and communication when introducing new workflows or systems.
Ensure teams successfully adopt process improvements and automation solutions.

Required Skills & Experience

3–5+ years of experience
in project management, operations, process improvement, or systems implementation.
Proven experience managing cross-functional projects from planning through execution.
Strong understanding of workflow optimization, process mapping, and operational efficiency.
Familiarity with automation tools such as n8n, Make, Zapier
, or similar platforms.
Proficiency with project management tools such as Asana, Monday.com, ClickUp, or Notion
.
Experience developing SOPs, gathering requirements, and coordinating system implementations.
Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
Excellent written and verbal English communication skills.
Ability to work independently, manage competing priorities, and collaborate with remote teams.

What Makes You Exceptional

You see inefficiencies and immediately start thinking about better ways to work.
You understand that successful projects require execution, not just planning.
You can translate complex operational challenges into clear, actionable solutions.
You are comfortable working with technical teams without needing to be a developer.
You proactively identify risks, communicate progress, and keep projects moving.
You measure success by actual business improvements, not just completed tasks.

Why This Role Matters

As Carepod grows, operational efficiency becomes increasingly important.
This role will help us scale smarter by reducing manual work, improving collaboration, and implementing processes that support sustainable growth.

You will play a key role in transforming how our teams operate, ensuring that improvements translate into measurable results across the business.

jobs.description:
We are looking for a talented Business Risk Intelligence Analyst
to join our team specializing in Systems/Information Technology
for our Corporate
organization in Columbus, IN.

In this role, you will make an impact in the following ways:

Lead cybersecurity risk identification and assessment efforts by applying Cummins risk management frameworks to proactively identify, evaluate, and mitigate security threats.
Serve as a trusted advisor to business and technology stakeholders, providing expert cybersecurity guidance for new and evolving technology solutions.
Drive the implementation of cybersecurity policies, data privacy principles, and industry best practices to protect organizational assets and information.
Translate cybersecurity frameworks such as NIST, ISO, ITIL, and COBIT into practical controls and processes that align with Cummins' business objectives.
Partner with cross-functional teams to evaluate technology changes, ensuring security requirements are incorporated early in the decision-making process.
Coach, mentor, and develop less experienced team members, strengthening the overall cybersecurity capabilities of the organization.
Build and maintain strong stakeholder relationships, leveraging Business Relationship Management practices to deliver measurable business value.
Influence risk-based decision-making by helping leaders understand cybersecurity risks, prioritize mitigation strategies, and balance security with business needs.

To be successful in this role you will need the following:

Action oriented - Taking on new opportunities and tough challenges with a sense of urgency, high energy, and enthusiasm.

Balances stakeholders - Anticipating and balancing the needs of multiple stakeholders.

Business insight - Applying knowledge of business and the marketplace to advance the organization’s goals.

Ensures accountability - Holding self and others accountable to meet commitments.

Manages complexity - Making sense of complex, high quantity, and sometimes contradictory information to effectively solve problems.

Organizational savvy - Maneuvering comfortably through complex policy, process, and people-related organizational dynamics.

Persuades - Using compelling arguments to gain the support and commitment of others.

Resourcefulness - Securing and deploying resources effectively and efficiently.

Tech savvy - Anticipating and adopting innovations in business-building digital and technology applications.

Training Delivery - Instructs learners in a manner that engages and adjusts to individual and group needs resulting in knowledge, skills and abilities that can be applied on the job.

Cybersecurity Risk Management - Identifies and assesses the potential impact of Cybersecurity risks against established Cybersecurity industry frameworks, regulations and organizational policies to develop and implement risk mitigation strategies in alignment with business objectives.

Regulatory Risk Compliance Management - Evaluates the design and effectiveness of controls against established industry frameworks and regulations to assess adherence with legal/regulatory requirements.

Values differences - Recognizing the value that different perspectives and cultures bring to an organization.

Education, Licenses, Certifications

College, university, or equivalent degree in Cybersecurity, Computer Science, or Information Technology, or related subject, or relevant equivalent experience required. This position may require licensing for compliance with export controls or sanctions regulations.

Experience

Intermediate level of relevant work experience required. 3-5 years of experience

Risk Intelligence Analysis

Analyze cyber, technology, and operational risk information to identify emerging risks and potential business impacts.
Assess internal and external intelligence to support proactive risk identification and executive decision-making.
Translate technical findings into business-focused intelligence for leadership.

Emerging Risk Monitoring

Monitor internal and external environments for emerging cyber, technology, regulatory, geopolitical, and operational risks.
Identify trends, patterns, and leading indicators that could impact enterprise objectives.
Support early warning activities through continuous intelligence collection and analysis.

Risk Correlation

Correlate information from cybersecurity operations, vulnerability management, threat intelligence, audit, compliance, enterprise risk, and business functions.
Identify relationships between risk events, business impacts, and strategic priorities.
Support development of enterprise Key Risk Indicators (KRIs) and Early Warning Indicators (EWIs).

Intelligence Reporting

Develop executive risk briefings, intelligence reports, trend analyses, and emerging risk assessments.
Produce decision-ready intelligence tailored for executive leadership, governance committees, and business stakeholders.
Contribute to quarterly and annual Business Risk Intelligence reporting.

Risk Assessment & Decision Support

Support enterprise risk assessments by evaluating likelihood, business impact, and potential mitigation strategies.
Assist leadership in prioritizing risks based on business context and organizational objectives.
Contribute to scenario analysis and strategic risk planning activities.

Collaboration & Continuous Improvement

Partner with Cybersecurity, Enterprise Risk Management, Audit, Compliance, Privacy, Legal, IT, and business teams to gather and validate intelligence.
Continuously improve intelligence methodologies, reporting standards, and analytical processes.
Leverage AI-enabled tools and analytics to improve the efficiency, quality, and timeliness of intelligence products while ensuring appropriate human oversight.

Bachelor’s degree in Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Information Systems, Intelligence Studies, Risk Management, or related field. Experience in cybersecurity, threat intelligence, risk analysis, or enterprise risk management. Knowledge of cyber threats, vulnerability management, risk frameworks, MITRE ATT&CK, threat intelligence, and business risk concepts preferred.

jobs.title: Principal Intelligence Analyst
jobs.description:
About the Aged Care Quality and Safety Commission

The Aged Care Quality and Safety Commission is the national regulator of Australian Government-funded aged care services.

We protect and enhance the safety, health, wellbeing, and quality of life of people receiving aged care. This includes managing complaints and feedback about the care older people receive.

We help build confidence and trust in aged care, by promoting best practice and a culture of safety and quality in the sector. We register providers and hold them to account if they don’t meet expected standards of care.

We work with providers, workers, older people, their families, and supporters to make sure they understand and uphold older people’s rights.

Meet some of our people and learn more about the Commission and our Regulatory Strategy on our website www.agedcarequality.gov.au

About the Team

The Data, Analytics and Intelligence (DAI) Branch
manages and analyses data from the aged care sector and regulatory activities to understand risks and performance for the purposes of prioritising and informing preventative and responsive risk treatments and regulatory decision making.

DAI’s role is to identify risks and guide decisions that inform preventative and responsive risk treatments. DAI supports service delivery through authoritative data and intelligence practice that is contemporary and compliant with relevant legislation, regulations, standards and aligned with the strategic imperatives of the Commission.

The Intelligence and Analytics Section delivers a risk profiling, intelligence and analytics program that empowers the Commission to manage sector, provider and worker risk. The section supports decision-making across the risk management lifecycle, including:

delivering integrated risk models and AI tools that flag potential harms before they occur
providing systemic insight and guiding responses on sector-wide risks
developing intelligence on risk trends and drivers of harm for aged care workers, providers and the sector.

The section’s trusted insights are founded on advanced analytical techniques, integrated data and the multi-disciplinary skillsets of data science, analytics and intelligence.

About the Role

The Principal Intelligence Analyst is the senior intelligence specialist and operational delivery lead for the Regulatory Intelligence team. Working under the direction of the Assistant Director, the role leads execution of the Regulatory Intelligence Strategy through the coordinated delivery of timely, objective and actionable intelligence products.

The role exercises operational authority over intelligence intake, triage, sequencing and analytical delivery. It leads complex and high-priority analytical work, integrates analytical workstreams, provides authoritative quality assurance and advice, and supports the embedding of agreed intelligence governance, standards and methodologies. The role provides professional leadership, mentoring and task coordination, but does not have primary responsibility for staff performance management, workforce allocation or formal team leadership.

Key Accountabilities include:

Lead execution of agreed Regulatory Intelligence Strategy priorities by converting intelligence requirements into coordinated analytical activities, products and delivery timeframes.
Lead complex Strategic Intelligence Assessments and other high-priority intelligence products, including defining analytical approaches, directing contributing workstreams and ensuring judgements are evidence-based and defensible.
Oversee the end-to-end flow of intelligence work, including intake, triage, sequencing, dependencies, milestones and the redirection of analytical effort in response to emerging intelligence and changing priorities.
Provide authoritative quality assurance and peer review to ensure intelligence products are clearly expressed, appropriately caveated and fit for executive and regulatory decision-making.
Integrate intelligence from regulatory activity, internal data, stakeholder engagement, open sources and partner agencies, and translate findings into practical implications, options and recommended actions.
Build trusted relationships and provide professional leadership, coaching and mentoring while embedding agreed governance, standards, methodologies, product frameworks and capability initiatives.

Position Eligibility Requirements (Selection Criteria) :

To be successful in this role you will need to demonstrate the following:
Demonstrated experience leading complex intelligence analysis and producing high-quality strategic or operational intelligence products for executive, regulatory or risk-based decision-making.
Excellent research, conceptual thinking, analytical and problem-solving skills, including sound judgement when evaluating incomplete, ambiguous, sensitive or contested information and applying structured analytical techniques.
Strong ability to execute agreed strategic priorities through coordinated analytical delivery, including triaging requirements, directing analytical effort, integrating workstreams and managing competing demands and dependencies.
Excellent written and oral communication skills, including concise and influential briefings and rigorous quality assurance for senior and diverse audiences.
Strong stakeholder engagement and professional leadership skills, including building productive relationships, negotiating priorities, coordinating specialist effort, mentoring staff and constructively challenging assumptions.
Strong regulatory intelligence and data literacy, integrity and professional courage, including appropriate handling of sensitive information and operation within legislative, policy and information-governance requirements.

Position Details

This is an ongoing role. A talent pool may be created for use in future recruitments. Any non-ongoing opportunities will be offered for a specified term. Opportunities will be offered for varying periods up to 12 months with the possibility of extension to a maximum of 24 months.
Merit Pool may be established through this selection process which may be used to fill this or future similar vacancies. Only candidates who hold Australian citizenship can apply.
Successful candidates must be willing to undertake a pre-employment screening.

Applications are to be submitted via the Aged Care Quality and Safety Commission Careers page.
Refer to our guidelines for candidate use of Artificial Intelligence (AI)
throughout the recruitment process.

jobs.title: PIR Technical Intelligence Analyst
jobs.description:
Modern Technology Solutions, Inc. (MTSI) is a 100% employee-owned engineering services and solutions company delivering high-demand technical expertise in digital transformation, modeling and simulation, rapid capability development, test and evaluation, artificial intelligence, autonomy, cybersecurity, and mission assurance. MTSI partners with government and industry customers to solve complex technical challenges and advance critical national security missions.

Position Overview

MTSI is seeking a PIR Technical Intelligence Analyst to support space and missile-related technical intelligence missions. The successful candidate will analyze infrared (IR) sensor data, characterize observed events and signatures, assess sensor performance, and develop technical intelligence products that support mission requirements.

Key Responsibilities

Analyze OPIR data, formatted event data, and infrared signatures to characterize missile events and other relevant phenomena.
Develop technical intelligence reports, target profiles, signature assessments, and supporting analytical products.
Evaluate sensor performance, including radiometric, temporal, and spectral characteristics.
Perform quality control and validation of analytical data and finished products.
Improve analytical methods, data processing, workflows, and automation to increase efficiency and product quality.
Prepare technical reports, briefings, and recommendations for Government customers.
Support the development, testing, and transition of analytical tools and capabilities.
Document analytical procedures and develop training materials to support mission continuity.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in engineering, physics, mathematics, remote sensing, or a related technical field.
At least five years of relevant experience in technical intelligence, OPIR analysis, sensor data analysis, or a related discipline.
Experience analyzing complex technical data and communicating findings through clear, well-supported reports.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and technical writing skills.

jobs.title: Senior Strategic Intelligence Analyst
jobs.description:
Summary

Mortenson is seeking a Senior Strategic Intelligence Analyst to join our Market Intelligence team. This is a research-intensive role for someone who enjoys digging into complex business questions, finding and evaluating information from many different sources, and turning that research into clear, compelling insights for senior leaders.

Desk research is at the heart of this position. You will investigate industries, markets, competitors, economic conditions, and emerging trends using public and subscription-based data, industry research, company information, news sources, and internal resources. You will determine what information is credible, what the evidence collectively says, and what matters for the business.

You will synthesize quantitative and qualitative information, develop well-supported points of view, and translate complex topics into concise executive reports, briefings, and presentations. This is a strategic intelligence role centered on research, analysis, synthesis, and business writing, not dashboard development or primary market research.

Responsibilities

Research and Analysis

Conduct in-depth desk research on industries, geographic markets, competitors, economic conditions, customers, and emerging business trends.
Find, evaluate, and synthesize quantitative and qualitative information from multiple credible sources.
Investigate ambiguous business questions, determine what information is needed, and develop clear, evidence-based conclusions.
Identify important trends, market shifts, risks, and opportunities and assess their implications for the business.
Develop deep knowledge of select markets, industries, competitors, and strategic topics through ongoing research and monitoring.

Strategic Intelligence and Executive Communications

Author market intelligence reports, executive briefings, market and sector outlooks, competitive analyses, and other strategic intelligence deliverables.
Turn extensive research and analysis into concise narratives that explain what is happening, why it matters, and what could happen next.
Combine narrative, data, charts, and exhibits to communicate complex topics simply and accurately.
Develop clear points of view while distinguishing evidence, interpretation, and implications.
Apply strong business judgment to surface the findings most relevant to senior leaders and strategic decisions.

Market and Competitive Intelligence

Analyze competitor strategies, capabilities, positioning, investments, and market activity to identify meaningful changes in the competitive landscape.
Monitor economic, construction, customer, and industry developments and connect external events to potential business implications.
Serve as an intelligence lead for select markets or strategic topics, developing expertise and maintaining an ongoing point of view.
Support business planning, growth strategy, market prioritization, and other strategic decisions with fact-based analysis.
Use AI and emerging research tools thoughtfully to accelerate research and synthesis while independently evaluating sources and conclusions.

You may be a good fit for this role if you enjoy digging into unfamiliar industries and business questions, finding credible evidence, connecting ideas across sources, and developing a point of view. You are as comfortable interpreting a chart or dataset as you are writing a clear executive narrative, and you take pride in turning complicated research into something a senior leader can understand quickly.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Business, Economics, Finance, Strategy, Journalism, Public Policy, Real Estate, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
Minimum seven years of experience in market intelligence, competitive intelligence, economic or industry research, strategy, consulting, or another analytically rigorous research environment.
Experience in nonresidential construction, commercial real estate, infrastructure, industrial markets, or another asset-intensive B2B industry strongly preferred
Demonstrated experience conducting complex business or industry research and developing clear, evidence-based conclusions.
Exceptional business writing and synthesis skills, including the ability to turn extensive research into concise executive narratives.
Strong business judgment and ability to distinguish an interesting fact from an insight that could influence a decision.
Strong quantitative literacy and ability to interpret market, economic, financial, and industry data.
Advanced PowerPoint skills and strong Excel proficiency, including the ability to create clear charts, exhibits, and executive-ready presentations.
Ability to travel approximately 10%

2+ years of experience in analytics within a pharmacy, PBM, or health plan setting.

Strong problem-solving skills, including the ability to investigate discrepancies and identify root causes.
Strong communication and organizational skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and requests.
Willingness to learn and apply new systems and tools, including approved automation or AI-assisted tools, while independently validating all outputs.
A high level of discretion and the ability to maintain confidentiality.
Comfort working in a fast-paced environment with evolving priorities.

Bonus Points For

Snowflake experience.
Experience building or maintaining dashboards or BI reporting in Power BI, Tableau, or similar tools.
Reporting and trend analysis experience.
Experience with Medi-Span or other drug-reference data.
Exposure to pharmacy rebate, formulary, or financial reporting.

Why Expion, Why Now

This is a pivotal moment to join Expion. Our data and analytics sit at the center of how we deliver value to clients, and accurate, dependable pharmacy analytics is what makes our insight credible. As a Data Analyst, Pharmacy Analytics, you won't just deliver reports; you'll help set the standard for data quality, documentation, and automation as we grow.

Our values say it best: Build boldly, improve relentlessly

This is a newly created position offering the opportunity to help shape and mature cyber security capabilities across corporate IT, Operational Technology (OT) and Internet of Things (IoT) environments. Working closely with the Enterprise Infrastructure Manager, you will play a key role in strengthening security controls, managing risk, improving resilience and supporting critical business operations.

About The Role

As the Cyber Security Analyst, you will be responsible for the design, implementation and ongoing support of cyber security controls across a diverse technology landscape.

You will work across security engineering, vulnerability management, compliance, incident response and continuous improvement initiatives, helping to build a robust and scalable cyber security capability.

Security Engineering & Operations

Provide security guidance and mentoring to technical and business stakeholders.

Skills & Experience

Hands-on experience with key security technologies including:

Knowledge of Linux environments and enterprise mobility platforms.
Excellent communication, stakeholder engagement and problem-solving skills.
Ability to assess, communicate and manage cyber security risks.

Highly Regarded

Experience working within Operational Technology (OT), industrial or critical infrastructure environments.
DevSecOps, automation and orchestration experience.
Exposure to cloud security and infrastructure security engineering.
Experience mentoring or providing technical leadership within security teams.

Qualifications

Degree in Cyber Security, Information Technology, Engineering or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
Industry certifications such as CISSP, CISM, Security+, Azure Security, GIAC or equivalent will be highly regarded.
Minimum 3 years' experience in cyber security-focused roles.
Demonstrated experience working with frameworks such as Essential Eight, NIST, ISA/IEC 62443 or AESCSF.

If you're a hands-on Cyber Security professional looking for an opportunity to make a significant impact and help shape the future security posture of a complex organisation, we'd love to hear from you.

jobs.title: Principal Intelligence Analyst
jobs.description:
About the Aged Care Quality and Safety Commission

The Aged Care Quality and Safety Commission is the national regulator of Australian Government-funded aged care services.

We protect and enhance the safety, health, wellbeing, and quality of life of people receiving aged care. This includes managing complaints and feedback about the care older people receive.

We help build confidence and trust in aged care, by promoting best practice and a culture of safety and quality in the sector. We register providers and hold them to account if they don’t meet expected standards of care.

We work with providers, workers, older people, their families, and supporters to make sure they understand and uphold older people’s rights.

Meet some of our people and learn more about the Commission and our Regulatory Strategy on our website www.agedcarequality.gov.au

About the Team

The Data, Analytics and Intelligence (DAI) Branch
manages and analyses data from the aged care sector and regulatory activities to understand risks and performance for the purposes of prioritising and informing preventative and responsive risk treatments and regulatory decision making.

DAI’s role is to identify risks and guide decisions that inform preventative and responsive risk treatments. DAI supports service delivery through authoritative data and intelligence practice that is contemporary and compliant with relevant legislation, regulations, standards and aligned with the strategic imperatives of the Commission.

The Intelligence and Analytics Section delivers a risk profiling, intelligence and analytics program that empowers the Commission to manage sector, provider and worker risk. The section supports decision-making across the risk management lifecycle, including:

delivering integrated risk models and AI tools that flag potential harms before they occur
providing systemic insight and guiding responses on sector-wide risks
developing intelligence on risk trends and drivers of harm for aged care workers, providers and the sector.

The section’s trusted insights are founded on advanced analytical techniques, integrated data and the multi-disciplinary skillsets of data science, analytics and intelligence.

About the Role

The Principal Intelligence Analyst is the senior intelligence specialist and operational delivery lead for the Regulatory Intelligence team. Working under the direction of the Assistant Director, the role leads execution of the Regulatory Intelligence Strategy through the coordinated delivery of timely, objective and actionable intelligence products.

The role exercises operational authority over intelligence intake, triage, sequencing and analytical delivery. It leads complex and high-priority analytical work, integrates analytical workstreams, provides authoritative quality assurance and advice, and supports the embedding of agreed intelligence governance, standards and methodologies. The role provides professional leadership, mentoring and task coordination, but does not have primary responsibility for staff performance management, workforce allocation or formal team leadership.

Key Accountabilities include:

Lead execution of agreed Regulatory Intelligence Strategy priorities by converting intelligence requirements into coordinated analytical activities, products and delivery timeframes.
Lead complex Strategic Intelligence Assessments and other high-priority intelligence products, including defining analytical approaches, directing contributing workstreams and ensuring judgements are evidence-based and defensible.
Oversee the end-to-end flow of intelligence work, including intake, triage, sequencing, dependencies, milestones and the redirection of analytical effort in response to emerging intelligence and changing priorities.
Provide authoritative quality assurance and peer review to ensure intelligence products are clearly expressed, appropriately caveated and fit for executive and regulatory decision-making.
Integrate intelligence from regulatory activity, internal data, stakeholder engagement, open sources and partner agencies, and translate findings into practical implications, options and recommended actions.
Build trusted relationships and provide professional leadership, coaching and mentoring while embedding agreed governance, standards, methodologies, product frameworks and capability initiatives.

Position Eligibility Requirements (Selection Criteria) :

To be successful in this role you will need to demonstrate the following:
Demonstrated experience leading complex intelligence analysis and producing high-quality strategic or operational intelligence products for executive, regulatory or risk-based decision-making.
Excellent research, conceptual thinking, analytical and problem-solving skills, including sound judgement when evaluating incomplete, ambiguous, sensitive or contested information and applying structured analytical techniques.
Strong ability to execute agreed strategic priorities through coordinated analytical delivery, including triaging requirements, directing analytical effort, integrating workstreams and managing competing demands and dependencies.
Excellent written and oral communication skills, including concise and influential briefings and rigorous quality assurance for senior and diverse audiences.
Strong stakeholder engagement and professional leadership skills, including building productive relationships, negotiating priorities, coordinating specialist effort, mentoring staff and constructively challenging assumptions.
Strong regulatory intelligence and data literacy, integrity and professional courage, including appropriate handling of sensitive information and operation within legislative, policy and information-governance requirements.

Position Details

This is an ongoing role. A talent pool may be created for use in future recruitments. Any non-ongoing opportunities will be offered for a specified term. Opportunities will be offered for varying periods up to 12 months with the possibility of extension to a maximum of 24 months.
Merit Pool may be established through this selection process which may be used to fill this or future similar vacancies. Only candidates who hold Australian citizenship can apply.
Successful candidates must be willing to undertake a pre-employment screening.

Applications are to be submitted via the Aged Care Quality and Safety Commission Careers page.
Refer to our guidelines for candidate use of Artificial Intelligence (AI)
throughout the recruitment process.

jobs.description:
Company Description

Goosehead Insurance is redefining the insurance brokerage industry with a vibrant, fast-paced culture built on innovation, agility, and exponential growth. As one of America’s fastest-growing independent insurance agencies, Goosehead leverages cutting-edge technology (both proprietary and third-party) and data-driven strategies to transform the client experience.
Despite being a public company, Goosehead maintains its entrepreneurial spirit and startup mentality. This creates endless opportunities for team members eager to make an impact, drive strategic initiatives, and shape the future of the insurance landscape.
We cultivate a collaborative, high-energy environment where leaders are empowered to take bold decisions and build remarkable teams. At Goosehead, ambition meets fun as we scale rapidly and challenge conventional industry norms, setting new standards for excellence. This is a place where employees can really craft their careers — endless opportunities!
Join us in writing Goosehead’s next chapter!

About the Role

Goosehead is turning its in-house Service organization into a product: we’re packaging our servicing capability and offering it to other P&C brokerages as a sub-servicing solution. As the Business Analyst on this team, you’ll be the analytical backbone of that new business — sizing the opportunity, tracking performance, and helping build the playbook that lets us stand it up, scale it, and run it well.

This is a hands-on operations analyst role, not a consulting role. You’ll spend your days in the data, close to the team doing the work, and close to the leaders making the calls. You’ll help set targets, monitor how we’re doing against them, surface where things are breaking, and support performance conversations with concrete numbers. You’ll also help design the operating model itself — staffing math, SLAs, pricing inputs, escalation paths — as we take a service that has only ever been run internally and make it work for external clients.

What you’ll do

Build and maintain the sizing models that inform staffing, capacity, and pricing as we onboard new brokerage partners
Own the operational dashboards and KPIs for the sub-servicing team — volume, SLAs, quality, productivity, client health — and make sure leaders see what they need, when they need it
Track team and individual performance; partner with team leads to translate the numbers into coaching, staffing, and process decisions
Help design and continually refine the playbook for standing up sub-servicing — onboarding new brokerage clients, ramping staff, defining SLAs, handling escalations, and closing out issues
Analyze operational data (ticket volumes, handle times, error rates, client satisfaction) to find where the team is losing time or quality, and propose fixes
Support pricing and unit-economics work — what does it cost us to service a policy, an account, a book — and how that should translate into what we charge
Build the reporting we share with brokerage clients so they trust what they’re getting
Partner with Service leadership, Operations, Finance, and Technology to turn analysis into changes that actually get implemented
Keep the work grounded and practical — clear spreadsheets, tight one-pagers, and answers people can act on

Experience and Qualifications

3+ years of experience in business analysis, operations analytics, FP&A, or a similar analytical role — ideally in a services, operations, or contact-center-adjacent environment
Strong Excel skills — you’re comfortable building models from scratch, not just editing someone else’s
Comfort with operational and performance data: capacity planning, throughput, SLAs, quality metrics
Ability to turn messy operational data into clear insights and specific recommendations
Solid communication skills — you can walk a team lead through their numbers or brief a VP on where the risk is, and adjust for the audience
Practical, get-it-done mindset — you’re happy owning the work end-to-end in a fast-moving environment
Experience with SQL, a BI tool (Tableau, Power BI, Looker), or Salesforce reporting is a plus

Preferred (not required)

Experience supporting a service, operations, or contact-center team — particularly around performance management, SLA reporting, or workforce planning
Experience helping stand up a new team, product, or line of business (not just running one that already exists)
Familiarity with P&C insurance, agency operations, or BPO / sub-servicing models
Exposure to unit economics, pricing, or margin analysis in a services business

Lifestyle and Work Environment

Based in Westlake, TX (in-office 5 days a week)
Typical schedule: 8:30am–5:30pm, with a commitment to flexibility and autonomy
Access to a great fitness center within the office facility

This position requires a unique blend of technical expertise and executive-level strategic thinking. This role contributes to strategic research, assessments, data analysis, roadmap development, and the preparation of materials that support executive decision ‑ making for large-scale enterprise IT initiatives. Serving as the primary backup to the Technical Strategy Lead, the ideal candidate has strong analytical capabilities, can synthesize complex IT infrastructure information into clear insights, and is comfortable working in a fast ‑ paced CAG environment.

This role is on-site at the Navy Yard in Washington, D.C.

An active Secret clearance is required.

Roles And Responsibilities

Strategy Analysis & Research

Conduct research and analysis on technology trends, capability gaps, and mission requirements related to enterprise IT environments and systems.
Evaluate emerging IT capabilities (e.g., cloud architectures, Zero Trust, DevSecOps, automation) for relevance to the acquisition program.
Develop summaries, insights, and recommendations that inform the Program Director's strategic direction.

Roadmap & Planning Support

Assist in developing multi ‑ year enterprise IT roadmaps, including sequencing, dependencies, and key acquisition milestones.
Maintain and update strategy artifacts, including concept papers, decision briefs, IT vision documents, and alignment frameworks.
Support the integration of technical strategy with engineering, cybersecurity, operations, and program management workstreams.

Stakeholder Engagement & Collaboration

Partner with the Technical Strategy Lead to support workshops, working sessions, and leadership forums focused on enterprise IT strategy development and alignment.
Gather inputs from stakeholders across technical, operational, and business areas of the Program.
Consolidate feedback and help refine strategy recommendations based on stakeholder insights and acquisition program needs.
Serve as the designated alternate for the Technical Strategy Lead, representing the CAG and the Program Director's interests in senior-level technical and strategic forums during their absence.

Data Analysis & Insight Generation

Analyze qualitative and quantitative data related to IT service delivery, system performance, and enterprise technology adoption.
Develop charts, dashboards, and visualizations that communicate modernization trends, risks, and strategic opportunities.
Translate complex engineering and acquisition data into clear, actionable insights for executive leadership decision ‑ making.

Documentation & Executive Communication

Draft, synthesize, and refine strategy documents, white papers, decision briefs, and presentations for leadership evaluation.
Ensure technical IT materials are clear, concise, and tailored to senior audiences across classified and unclassified environments.

Required Qualifications

Active Secret Clearance
7+ years of experience in strategy analysis, digital transformation, enterprise technology, or related analytical roles (Navy preferred).
Strong analytical, research, and problem ‑ solving skills.
Ability to synthesize complex technical and mission ‑ related information into concise insights.

Comfortable working collaboratively with technical, operational, and leadership stakeholders.

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Systems Engineering, Cybersecurity, or a highly related technical discipline. Relevant experience (4+ years in addition to required) may be substituted for degree.
3+ years of demonstrated experience within DoD IT acquisition programs.
