Founded in 2011 and backed by a leading private equity firm, we partner with best-in-class practices across our industry to co-own and accelerate their growth—while preserving the unique identity and culture that made them successful. Our model delivers industry-leading growth and profitability. We centralize back-office operations, drive sustained revenue expansion, and equip our partners with the infrastructure and expertise they need—so they can focus on delivering exceptional patient care while retaining ownership in their lifelong practices.

Today, we operate in 30+ states and are growing rapidly. We are a lean, high-performance team of operators, investors, and entrepreneurs united by a belief that our sector is ripe for thoughtful disruption and operational excellence.

About the Role

The Strategic Operations Manager
is a high-impact business leader operating as a “mini-CEO” for a defined region, directly accountable for value creation, profitability, and operational performance. Reporting to the COO or VP of Operations, this role blends strategy and execution—owning multi-site P&L performance while driving initiatives that accelerate growth and improve operational rigor.

This cross-functional position is ideal for candidates from management consulting, investment banking, or private equity backgrounds who are eager to step into true operating ownership within a fast-growing, sponsor-backed environment. You will collaborate closely with local partners while engaging regularly with senior leadership—including the CEO, Operations, Marketing, Finance and Strategy —on high-impact initiatives. You will translate data into action, align stakeholders around clear priorities, and ensure measurable results at the facility level.

Success in this role requires strong financial acumen, emotional intelligence, multi-site operating discipline, and the ability to drive buy-in across diverse stakeholders.

This position offers:
Direct P&L ownership
Meaningful executive exposure
Accelerated development across strategy and operations
Significant upward mobility within a high-growth organization

Own regional performance, driving revenue growth, cost optimization, and overall value creation.

Conduct comprehensive facility assessments to identify inefficiencies, bottlenecks, and growth opportunities.
Implement best practices across operations, leveraging technology and process improvements where appropriate.
Partner cross-functionally with Operations, Strategy, Marketing, Finance, and Executive Leadership on strategic initiatives and special projects.
Develop and empower regional teams through training, coaching, and performance management.
Build trusted relationships with local partners to ensure alignment, execution excellence, and cultural cohesion.

Experience in a highly analytical environment (e.g., management consulting, private equity, investment banking, corporate strategy) with exposure to senior leadership.

Entrepreneurial, results-oriented mindset with the ability to balance strategic thinking and hands-on execution.
Exceptional communication and relationship-building skills, with the emotional intelligence to influence across all levels of the organization.

Overall responsibility for all works taking place on site, leading pre-planning meetings between the Mercury & supply chain partner teams to review & understand all aspects of the required deliverables ensuring compliance with Mercury & client procedures.
Work closely with the Project Director/Manager & Commercial Manager as part of the project triumvirate, ensuring all KPI’s are delivered. Ensure adequate resources are in place, in line with agreed budgets, to maintain the site conditions in line with expectations. Lead the way on promotion of a strong EHS & Quality culture on site through attendance at Whiteboard, DABS, Last Planner, Collaborative Planning & SLT meetings.
Champion the site culture on SOP recording & close out of items raised.

Focus on delivery of the “Bringing Quality 2 Life” & “Right First Time” initiatives by supporting package leads with supply chain partner understanding & involvement.

Maintain an up-to-date awareness of the project commercial status through collaboration with the commercial team. Ensure any scope changes are communicated to allow recovery through the change management process.
Maintain positive working relationships with our supply chain partners, listening to their concerns & resolving any issues promptly.

Weekly client meeting
Weekly operations interface meeting
Weekly internal meeting
Weekly schedule meeting
Monthly SLT meeting
Whiteboard, DABS, Collaborative & Last planner meetings

Engineering Degree or recognised trade qualification

The Role
WHSmith North America is looking for an experienced Senior IT Project Manager to lead the delivery of technology projects across our North American retail estate.

Lead IT projects from initial requirements and planning through implementation, cutover, handover and closure.

Identify project risks and issues early and drive them through to resolution.
Manage third-party suppliers against agreed deliverables, dates and service expectations.
Ensure project documentation, technical standards and governance requirements are followed.
Provide clear project status reporting to senior IT and business stakeholders.
Continually improve the standard approach, templates and processes used for retail technology deployments.

Point of Sale (POS)
Payment terminals and payment services
Store LAN, WAN and Wi-Fi
Internet and telecommunications circuits
Back-office systems
PCs, tablets and mobile devices
Printers and peripheral devices
Handheld scanners and inventory devices
Stock and inventory systems
Digital signage
CCTV, EAS and other technology supporting loss prevention
Store servers and edge technology where applicable
Device configuration and deployment

Technology asset management
Remote support and store support models

Design → Procurement → Connectivity → Installation → Configuration → Testing → Cutover → Opening → Hypercare → Handover

They should understand issues such as circuit lead times, equipment delivery, site access, construction dependencies, POS configuration, payment testing, stock-system readiness and opening-day support.

Experience should also include management of store closures, including:
Technology shutdown planning
Asset identification and recovery
Equipment redeployment
Network and telecom service termination
POS and payment device removal
Data/security considerations
Supplier coordination
Asset disposal
Updating configuration and asset-management records

Minimum 5 years’ experience delivering IT projects.

Experience managing multiple projects concurrently.
Experience managing third-party technology vendors.

Strong project planning, financial management, risk management and governance skills.
Experience working with both technology and operational business teams.
Excellent communication and stakeholder-management skills.
Comfortable working in a fast-paced operational retail environment.

Highly Desirable

Travel retail

Multi-site retail
Hospitality
High-volume retail environments
POS replacement programmes
Network/Wi-Fi deployments
Payment technology
Retail infrastructure refreshes
Large-scale store rollout programmes

Project Management Skills

Project planning and scheduling
Budget management
RAID management
Vendor management
Stakeholder management
Change control
Dependency management
Project governance
Executive reporting
Cutover planning
Operational readiness
Lessons learned and continuous improvement

PMP, PRINCE2, Agile or equivalent project-management qualifications would be beneficial but are less important than proven delivery experience.

Success in this role means stores open on time with technology that works from day one.

new_jobs.title: Principal Intelligence Analyst
new_jobs.description:
About the Aged Care Quality and Safety Commission

The Aged Care Quality and Safety Commission is the national regulator of Australian Government-funded aged care services.

We protect and enhance the safety, health, wellbeing, and quality of life of people receiving aged care. This includes managing complaints and feedback about the care older people receive.

We help build confidence and trust in aged care, by promoting best practice and a culture of safety and quality in the sector. We register providers and hold them to account if they don’t meet expected standards of care.

We work with providers, workers, older people, their families, and supporters to make sure they understand and uphold older people’s rights.

Meet some of our people and learn more about the Commission and our Regulatory Strategy on our website www.agedcarequality.gov.au

About the Team

The Data, Analytics and Intelligence (DAI) Branch
manages and analyses data from the aged care sector and regulatory activities to understand risks and performance for the purposes of prioritising and informing preventative and responsive risk treatments and regulatory decision making.

DAI’s role is to identify risks and guide decisions that inform preventative and responsive risk treatments. DAI supports service delivery through authoritative data and intelligence practice that is contemporary and compliant with relevant legislation, regulations, standards and aligned with the strategic imperatives of the Commission.

The Intelligence and Analytics Section delivers a risk profiling, intelligence and analytics program that empowers the Commission to manage sector, provider and worker risk. The section supports decision-making across the risk management lifecycle, including:

delivering integrated risk models and AI tools that flag potential harms before they occur
providing systemic insight and guiding responses on sector-wide risks
developing intelligence on risk trends and drivers of harm for aged care workers, providers and the sector.

The section’s trusted insights are founded on advanced analytical techniques, integrated data and the multi-disciplinary skillsets of data science, analytics and intelligence.

About the Role

The Principal Intelligence Analyst is the senior intelligence specialist and operational delivery lead for the Regulatory Intelligence team. Working under the direction of the Assistant Director, the role leads execution of the Regulatory Intelligence Strategy through the coordinated delivery of timely, objective and actionable intelligence products.

The role exercises operational authority over intelligence intake, triage, sequencing and analytical delivery. It leads complex and high-priority analytical work, integrates analytical workstreams, provides authoritative quality assurance and advice, and supports the embedding of agreed intelligence governance, standards and methodologies. The role provides professional leadership, mentoring and task coordination, but does not have primary responsibility for staff performance management, workforce allocation or formal team leadership.

Key Accountabilities include:

Lead execution of agreed Regulatory Intelligence Strategy priorities by converting intelligence requirements into coordinated analytical activities, products and delivery timeframes.
Lead complex Strategic Intelligence Assessments and other high-priority intelligence products, including defining analytical approaches, directing contributing workstreams and ensuring judgements are evidence-based and defensible.
Oversee the end-to-end flow of intelligence work, including intake, triage, sequencing, dependencies, milestones and the redirection of analytical effort in response to emerging intelligence and changing priorities.
Provide authoritative quality assurance and peer review to ensure intelligence products are clearly expressed, appropriately caveated and fit for executive and regulatory decision-making.
Integrate intelligence from regulatory activity, internal data, stakeholder engagement, open sources and partner agencies, and translate findings into practical implications, options and recommended actions.
Build trusted relationships and provide professional leadership, coaching and mentoring while embedding agreed governance, standards, methodologies, product frameworks and capability initiatives.

Position Eligibility Requirements (Selection Criteria) :

To be successful in this role you will need to demonstrate the following:
Demonstrated experience leading complex intelligence analysis and producing high-quality strategic or operational intelligence products for executive, regulatory or risk-based decision-making.
Excellent research, conceptual thinking, analytical and problem-solving skills, including sound judgement when evaluating incomplete, ambiguous, sensitive or contested information and applying structured analytical techniques.
Strong ability to execute agreed strategic priorities through coordinated analytical delivery, including triaging requirements, directing analytical effort, integrating workstreams and managing competing demands and dependencies.
Excellent written and oral communication skills, including concise and influential briefings and rigorous quality assurance for senior and diverse audiences.
Strong stakeholder engagement and professional leadership skills, including building productive relationships, negotiating priorities, coordinating specialist effort, mentoring staff and constructively challenging assumptions.
Strong regulatory intelligence and data literacy, integrity and professional courage, including appropriate handling of sensitive information and operation within legislative, policy and information-governance requirements.

Position Details

This is an ongoing role. A talent pool may be created for use in future recruitments. Any non-ongoing opportunities will be offered for a specified term. Opportunities will be offered for varying periods up to 12 months with the possibility of extension to a maximum of 24 months.
Merit Pool may be established through this selection process which may be used to fill this or future similar vacancies. Only candidates who hold Australian citizenship can apply.
Successful candidates must be willing to undertake a pre-employment screening.

Applications are to be submitted via the Aged Care Quality and Safety Commission Careers page.
Refer to our guidelines for candidate use of Artificial Intelligence (AI)
throughout the recruitment process.

Summary

Mortenson is seeking a Senior Strategic Intelligence Analyst to join our Market Intelligence team. This is a research-intensive role for someone who enjoys digging into complex business questions, finding and evaluating information from many different sources, and turning that research into clear, compelling insights for senior leaders.

Desk research is at the heart of this position. You will investigate industries, markets, competitors, economic conditions, and emerging trends using public and subscription-based data, industry research, company information, news sources, and internal resources. You will determine what information is credible, what the evidence collectively says, and what matters for the business.

You will synthesize quantitative and qualitative information, develop well-supported points of view, and translate complex topics into concise executive reports, briefings, and presentations. This is a strategic intelligence role centered on research, analysis, synthesis, and business writing, not dashboard development or primary market research.

Responsibilities

Research and Analysis

Conduct in-depth desk research on industries, geographic markets, competitors, economic conditions, customers, and emerging business trends.
Find, evaluate, and synthesize quantitative and qualitative information from multiple credible sources.
Investigate ambiguous business questions, determine what information is needed, and develop clear, evidence-based conclusions.
Identify important trends, market shifts, risks, and opportunities and assess their implications for the business.
Develop deep knowledge of select markets, industries, competitors, and strategic topics through ongoing research and monitoring.

Strategic Intelligence and Executive Communications

Author market intelligence reports, executive briefings, market and sector outlooks, competitive analyses, and other strategic intelligence deliverables.
Turn extensive research and analysis into concise narratives that explain what is happening, why it matters, and what could happen next.
Combine narrative, data, charts, and exhibits to communicate complex topics simply and accurately.
Develop clear points of view while distinguishing evidence, interpretation, and implications.
Apply strong business judgment to surface the findings most relevant to senior leaders and strategic decisions.

Market and Competitive Intelligence

Analyze competitor strategies, capabilities, positioning, investments, and market activity to identify meaningful changes in the competitive landscape.
Monitor economic, construction, customer, and industry developments and connect external events to potential business implications.
Serve as an intelligence lead for select markets or strategic topics, developing expertise and maintaining an ongoing point of view.
Support business planning, growth strategy, market prioritization, and other strategic decisions with fact-based analysis.
Use AI and emerging research tools thoughtfully to accelerate research and synthesis while independently evaluating sources and conclusions.

You may be a good fit for this role if you enjoy digging into unfamiliar industries and business questions, finding credible evidence, connecting ideas across sources, and developing a point of view. You are as comfortable interpreting a chart or dataset as you are writing a clear executive narrative, and you take pride in turning complicated research into something a senior leader can understand quickly.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Business, Economics, Finance, Strategy, Journalism, Public Policy, Real Estate, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
Minimum seven years of experience in market intelligence, competitive intelligence, economic or industry research, strategy, consulting, or another analytically rigorous research environment.

Exceptional business writing and synthesis skills, including the ability to turn extensive research into concise executive narratives.
Strong business judgment and ability to distinguish an interesting fact from an insight that could influence a decision.
Strong quantitative literacy and ability to interpret market, economic, financial, and industry data.
Advanced PowerPoint skills and strong Excel proficiency, including the ability to create clear charts, exhibits, and executive-ready presentations.
Ability to travel approximately 10%

new_jobs.title: Principal Intelligence Analyst
new_jobs.description:
About the Aged Care Quality and Safety Commission

The Aged Care Quality and Safety Commission is the national regulator of Australian Government-funded aged care services.

We protect and enhance the safety, health, wellbeing, and quality of life of people receiving aged care. This includes managing complaints and feedback about the care older people receive.

We help build confidence and trust in aged care, by promoting best practice and a culture of safety and quality in the sector. We register providers and hold them to account if they don’t meet expected standards of care.

We work with providers, workers, older people, their families, and supporters to make sure they understand and uphold older people’s rights.

Meet some of our people and learn more about the Commission and our Regulatory Strategy on our website www.agedcarequality.gov.au

About the Team

The Data, Analytics and Intelligence (DAI) Branch
manages and analyses data from the aged care sector and regulatory activities to understand risks and performance for the purposes of prioritising and informing preventative and responsive risk treatments and regulatory decision making.

DAI’s role is to identify risks and guide decisions that inform preventative and responsive risk treatments. DAI supports service delivery through authoritative data and intelligence practice that is contemporary and compliant with relevant legislation, regulations, standards and aligned with the strategic imperatives of the Commission.

The Intelligence and Analytics Section delivers a risk profiling, intelligence and analytics program that empowers the Commission to manage sector, provider and worker risk. The section supports decision-making across the risk management lifecycle, including:

delivering integrated risk models and AI tools that flag potential harms before they occur
providing systemic insight and guiding responses on sector-wide risks
developing intelligence on risk trends and drivers of harm for aged care workers, providers and the sector.

The section’s trusted insights are founded on advanced analytical techniques, integrated data and the multi-disciplinary skillsets of data science, analytics and intelligence.

About the Role

The Principal Intelligence Analyst is the senior intelligence specialist and operational delivery lead for the Regulatory Intelligence team. Working under the direction of the Assistant Director, the role leads execution of the Regulatory Intelligence Strategy through the coordinated delivery of timely, objective and actionable intelligence products.

The role exercises operational authority over intelligence intake, triage, sequencing and analytical delivery. It leads complex and high-priority analytical work, integrates analytical workstreams, provides authoritative quality assurance and advice, and supports the embedding of agreed intelligence governance, standards and methodologies. The role provides professional leadership, mentoring and task coordination, but does not have primary responsibility for staff performance management, workforce allocation or formal team leadership.

Key Accountabilities include:

Lead execution of agreed Regulatory Intelligence Strategy priorities by converting intelligence requirements into coordinated analytical activities, products and delivery timeframes.
Lead complex Strategic Intelligence Assessments and other high-priority intelligence products, including defining analytical approaches, directing contributing workstreams and ensuring judgements are evidence-based and defensible.
Oversee the end-to-end flow of intelligence work, including intake, triage, sequencing, dependencies, milestones and the redirection of analytical effort in response to emerging intelligence and changing priorities.
Provide authoritative quality assurance and peer review to ensure intelligence products are clearly expressed, appropriately caveated and fit for executive and regulatory decision-making.
Integrate intelligence from regulatory activity, internal data, stakeholder engagement, open sources and partner agencies, and translate findings into practical implications, options and recommended actions.
Build trusted relationships and provide professional leadership, coaching and mentoring while embedding agreed governance, standards, methodologies, product frameworks and capability initiatives.

Position Eligibility Requirements (Selection Criteria) :

To be successful in this role you will need to demonstrate the following:
Demonstrated experience leading complex intelligence analysis and producing high-quality strategic or operational intelligence products for executive, regulatory or risk-based decision-making.
Excellent research, conceptual thinking, analytical and problem-solving skills, including sound judgement when evaluating incomplete, ambiguous, sensitive or contested information and applying structured analytical techniques.
Strong ability to execute agreed strategic priorities through coordinated analytical delivery, including triaging requirements, directing analytical effort, integrating workstreams and managing competing demands and dependencies.
Excellent written and oral communication skills, including concise and influential briefings and rigorous quality assurance for senior and diverse audiences.
Strong stakeholder engagement and professional leadership skills, including building productive relationships, negotiating priorities, coordinating specialist effort, mentoring staff and constructively challenging assumptions.
Strong regulatory intelligence and data literacy, integrity and professional courage, including appropriate handling of sensitive information and operation within legislative, policy and information-governance requirements.

Position Details

This is an ongoing role. A talent pool may be created for use in future recruitments. Any non-ongoing opportunities will be offered for a specified term. Opportunities will be offered for varying periods up to 12 months with the possibility of extension to a maximum of 24 months.
Merit Pool may be established through this selection process which may be used to fill this or future similar vacancies. Only candidates who hold Australian citizenship can apply.
Successful candidates must be willing to undertake a pre-employment screening.

Applications are to be submitted via the Aged Care Quality and Safety Commission Careers page.
Refer to our guidelines for candidate use of Artificial Intelligence (AI)
throughout the recruitment process.

Company Description

Goosehead Insurance is redefining the insurance brokerage industry with a vibrant, fast-paced culture built on innovation, agility, and exponential growth. As one of America’s fastest-growing independent insurance agencies, Goosehead leverages cutting-edge technology (both proprietary and third-party) and data-driven strategies to transform the client experience.
Despite being a public company, Goosehead maintains its entrepreneurial spirit and startup mentality. This creates endless opportunities for team members eager to make an impact, drive strategic initiatives, and shape the future of the insurance landscape.
We cultivate a collaborative, high-energy environment where leaders are empowered to take bold decisions and build remarkable teams. At Goosehead, ambition meets fun as we scale rapidly and challenge conventional industry norms, setting new standards for excellence. This is a place where employees can really craft their careers — endless opportunities!
Join us in writing Goosehead’s next chapter!

About the Role

Goosehead is turning its in-house Service organization into a product: we’re packaging our servicing capability and offering it to other P&C brokerages as a sub-servicing solution. As the Business Analyst on this team, you’ll be the analytical backbone of that new business — sizing the opportunity, tracking performance, and helping build the playbook that lets us stand it up, scale it, and run it well.

This is a hands-on operations analyst role, not a consulting role. You’ll spend your days in the data, close to the team doing the work, and close to the leaders making the calls. You’ll help set targets, monitor how we’re doing against them, surface where things are breaking, and support performance conversations with concrete numbers. You’ll also help design the operating model itself — staffing math, SLAs, pricing inputs, escalation paths — as we take a service that has only ever been run internally and make it work for external clients.

What you’ll do

Build and maintain the sizing models that inform staffing, capacity, and pricing as we onboard new brokerage partners
Own the operational dashboards and KPIs for the sub-servicing team — volume, SLAs, quality, productivity, client health — and make sure leaders see what they need, when they need it
Track team and individual performance; partner with team leads to translate the numbers into coaching, staffing, and process decisions
Help design and continually refine the playbook for standing up sub-servicing — onboarding new brokerage clients, ramping staff, defining SLAs, handling escalations, and closing out issues
Analyze operational data (ticket volumes, handle times, error rates, client satisfaction) to find where the team is losing time or quality, and propose fixes
Support pricing and unit-economics work — what does it cost us to service a policy, an account, a book — and how that should translate into what we charge
Build the reporting we share with brokerage clients so they trust what they’re getting
Partner with Service leadership, Operations, Finance, and Technology to turn analysis into changes that actually get implemented
Keep the work grounded and practical — clear spreadsheets, tight one-pagers, and answers people can act on

Experience and Qualifications

3+ years of experience in business analysis, operations analytics, FP&A, or a similar analytical role — ideally in a services, operations, or contact-center-adjacent environment
Strong Excel skills — you’re comfortable building models from scratch, not just editing someone else’s
Comfort with operational and performance data: capacity planning, throughput, SLAs, quality metrics
Ability to turn messy operational data into clear insights and specific recommendations
Solid communication skills — you can walk a team lead through their numbers or brief a VP on where the risk is, and adjust for the audience
Practical, get-it-done mindset — you’re happy owning the work end-to-end in a fast-moving environment
Experience with SQL, a BI tool (Tableau, Power BI, Looker), or Salesforce reporting is a plus

Preferred (not required)

Experience supporting a service, operations, or contact-center team — particularly around performance management, SLA reporting, or workforce planning
Experience helping stand up a new team, product, or line of business (not just running one that already exists)
Familiarity with P&C insurance, agency operations, or BPO / sub-servicing models
Exposure to unit economics, pricing, or margin analysis in a services business

Lifestyle and Work Environment

Based in Westlake, TX (in-office 5 days a week)
Typical schedule: 8:30am–5:30pm, with a commitment to flexibility and autonomy
Access to a great fitness center within the office facility

new_jobs.title: Senior Technical Strategy Analyst
new_jobs.description:
The Sr. Technical Strategy Analyst serves a critical role within the Command Action Group (CAG), providing direct, high-level support to the Program Director and Deputy Director of a major DoD acquisition program. This position requires a unique blend of technical expertise and executive-level strategic thinking. This role contributes to strategic research, assessments, data analysis, roadmap development, and the preparation of materials that support executive decision ‑ making for large-scale enterprise IT initiatives. Serving as the primary backup to the Technical Strategy Lead, the ideal candidate has strong analytical capabilities, can synthesize complex IT infrastructure information into clear insights, and is comfortable working in a fast ‑ paced CAG environment.

This role is on-site at the Navy Yard in Washington, D.C.

An active Secret clearance is required.

Roles And Responsibilities

Strategy Analysis & Research

Conduct research and analysis on technology trends, capability gaps, and mission requirements related to enterprise IT environments and systems.
Evaluate emerging IT capabilities (e.g., cloud architectures, Zero Trust, DevSecOps, automation) for relevance to the acquisition program.
Develop summaries, insights, and recommendations that inform the Program Director's strategic direction.

Roadmap & Planning Support

Assist in developing multi ‑ year enterprise IT roadmaps, including sequencing, dependencies, and key acquisition milestones.
Maintain and update strategy artifacts, including concept papers, decision briefs, IT vision documents, and alignment frameworks.
Support the integration of technical strategy with engineering, cybersecurity, operations, and program management workstreams.

Stakeholder Engagement & Collaboration

Partner with the Technical Strategy Lead to support workshops, working sessions, and leadership forums focused on enterprise IT strategy development and alignment.
Gather inputs from stakeholders across technical, operational, and business areas of the Program.
Consolidate feedback and help refine strategy recommendations based on stakeholder insights and acquisition program needs.
Serve as the designated alternate for the Technical Strategy Lead, representing the CAG and the Program Director's interests in senior-level technical and strategic forums during their absence.

Data Analysis & Insight Generation

Analyze qualitative and quantitative data related to IT service delivery, system performance, and enterprise technology adoption.
Develop charts, dashboards, and visualizations that communicate modernization trends, risks, and strategic opportunities.
Translate complex engineering and acquisition data into clear, actionable insights for executive leadership decision ‑ making.

Documentation & Executive Communication

Draft, synthesize, and refine strategy documents, white papers, decision briefs, and presentations for leadership evaluation.
Ensure technical IT materials are clear, concise, and tailored to senior audiences across classified and unclassified environments.

Job Requirements

Required Qualifications

Active Secret Clearance
7+ years of experience in strategy analysis, digital transformation, enterprise technology, or related analytical roles (Navy preferred).
Strong analytical, research, and problem ‑ solving skills.
Ability to synthesize complex technical and mission ‑ related information into concise insights.
Experience preparing executive-level briefs, reports, and visualizations.
Comfortable working collaboratively with technical, operational, and leadership stakeholders.
Ability to work in classified environments and handle sensitive information appropriately.

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Systems Engineering, Cybersecurity, or a highly related technical discipline. Relevant experience (4+ years in addition to required) may be substituted for degree.
3+ years of demonstrated experience within DoD IT acquisition programs.
Advanced DAWIA certifications in Program Management or Engineering.
Familiarity with modern DoD IT initiatives, including DoD Zero Trust Architecture, Joint Warfighting Cloud Capability (JWCC), and the Software Acquisition Pathway.

The anticipated salary range for this role is $175,000 to $200,000 annually. The anticipated salary range for this position is provided in accordance with applicable pay transparency laws. The final starting salary will be determined based on a variety of job-related factors, including the selected candidate's qualifications, skills, relevant experience, education, certifications, and work location (where applicable), as well as internal equity and market considerations.

new_jobs.title: Senior Research Analyst, AI Transformation Best Practices
new_jobs.description:
Gravity Research is hiring a Senior Research Analyst
to help some of the world’s leading communications and corporate affairs teams navigate the rapidly changing world of AI.

This is a role for someone who is endlessly curious about what AI can do, eager to experiment with the latest tools, and excited to turn emerging ideas and peer experiences into practical solutions. You’ll work alongside senior executives to research how leading organizations move from simply experimenting with AI to fundamentally changing how their teams work, and help others follow their lead.

Gravity Research, born of National Journal, is a premier custom research and insights organization supporting corporate clients. Our mission is to help communications and corporate affairs leaders modernize their functions by finding where AI fits into their workflows and team structures.

Background

We are looking for curious and innovative researchers interested in helping communications and corporate affairs leaders smartly navigate AI’s transformation of their function through rigorous case study and best practices research.

The Role

Senior Analysts are responsible for contributing to all aspects of Gravity’s new AI transformation practice, with a focus on case study and best practices research. Analysts help communications and corporate affairs leaders move their teams from early experimentation to mature AI adoption. Analysts on this team use qualitative research methods to assess where organizations stand in their adoption journey, build step-by-step case studies and best practices, and create practical implementation guidance on how to modernize the function. Analysts work directly with senior leaders at Gravity and senior communications and corporate affairs executives at member organizations.

Qualifications Of The Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate is a strong qualitative researcher who is comfortable designing executive interviews and turning the findings into polished, practical insight. The candidate will also have hands-on comfort with AI tools and prompting, along with the curiosity to test how new tools can improve communications work. The candidate will have the ability to execute against tight deadlines to develop professional and intellectually sound deliverables for members, both independently and in close collaboration with team members.

Your Responsibilities Will Include

Designing in-depth interviews with senior executives and practitioners, and synthesizing the results into organized notes that capture key learnings.
Developing research using qualitative methods to synthesize findings from interviews, surveys, and open-source research into clear, actionable insights and best practices.
Writing and editing detailed step-by-step case studies and roadmaps that translate peer and expert insights into practical implementation plans clients can act on.
Constantly experimenting with new AI tools and releases to understand first-hand how they can be used to improve communications workflows.
Applying change management principles to help clients structure adoption roadmaps, training plans, and upskilling programs for teams navigating AI-enabled ways of working.
Drafting deliverables, including PowerPoint presentations, memos, and other formats, to communicate findings and recommendations to clients.
Supporting the design and delivery of monthly webinars, executive briefings, and training sessions that build AI capability across a client's team.
Preparing briefing materials and research summaries for executive advisors ahead of member meetings, and responding to subsequent questions.
Contributing to product development by crafting new and innovative approaches to producing the analytic work, optimizing operations, and perfecting the research product.
To perform this job successfully, each essential competency and responsibility must be performed satisfactorily. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable an individual with disabilities to perform essential functions. Other duties may be assigned to meet organizational goals.

Specific Qualifications Include

A highly analytic, natural problem solver.
Demonstrated experience conducting qualitative research, including designing interviews and synthesizing findings into clear conclusions.
The ability to highlight key insights within a complex set of data, synthesize large amounts of information, and then clearly explain these insights to clients.
Creative thinking and resourcefulness in problem-solving.
Experience creating case studies, benchmarking reports, white papers, or other client-facing research products is highly preferred.
A skilled project manager, able to independently manage competing priorities and adhere to timelines.
Familiarity with change management fundamentals and the ability to apply them practically to drive team adoption of new tools and workflows.
Hands-on experience using AI tools and prompting (e.g., ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot).
An individual with 1-3 years of experience in at least one of the following domains: case study or best practices research, change management, organizational development, AI transformation, or a related field.
Research focused on AI, organizational development, or the future of work preferred.
Earned Bachelor's degree required.
Entrepreneurial spirit; Track record of building new initiatives from conception to execution.
Prodigious work ethic and spirit of generosity.

$70,000 - $85,000 a year

The salary range for this role is $70,000-$85,000, commensurate with experience.

Start Date:
Available immediately

Employment Type:
Full-time

Location:
This job is based in Washington, DC. Gravity Research operates on a hybrid schedule, with employees required to be in the office every Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday.

______________________________________________________________________________________________________________

About Us

Across Gravity Research, generally, the firm looks for three “pillar gifts” in you, and everyone else. In all of us, these are more aspirational than actual, but they are central in our intentions –

Force of Ideas:
At the center of Gravity Research’s work are the ideas within our work. We believe that ideas—the good and not—have consequences. Our ultimate objective is to bring rigor, insight, and intellectual honesty to the goal of separating the bad from the good, and giving voice, argument, and flight to maintaining the latter.

Spirit of Generosity:
Gravity Research seeks in its ranks a spirit of generosity: a natural disposition in each colleague toward service and selfless conduct. Our writing should be cut from the same cloth—critical on the merits, but informed by charity and forbearance in measuring motive and personal character.

Radical Responsibility:
We give our people a lot of responsibility early on, and our top performers embrace it. We believe in holding ourselves and our colleagues accountable, taking ownership over big things, striving for excellence, and celebrating success.

Gravity Research is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We do not discriminate against our applicants because of race, color, religion, sex (including gender identity, sexual orientation, and pregnancy), national origin, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other status protected by applicable law.

We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses and identifying potential inconsistencies or verification signals in application materials based on available information. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us.

This highly visible principal individual contributor role requires the ability to move between organizational strategy, engineering detail, and hands-on implementation. You will independently lead ambiguous, cross-functional programs, translate business and regulatory needs into technical requirements, and build tooling that reduces manual work and improves delivery.

You will work closely with Engineering, Product, Quality, Legal, and Regulatory Affairs to integrate medical device requirements into development and operational workflows. A key focus will be using automation to improve requirements tracking, documentation, evidence collection, and readiness for regulatory reviews, audits, certifications, and product releases.

As a strategic partner to the Director of Operations, you will also support organizational planning, resource allocation, and executive decision-making. Success requires technical depth, sound judgment, and the ability to influence senior stakeholders while delivering measurable improvements across teams.

Responsibilities

What You’ll Do:

Lead Complex Technical Programs: Own cross-functional initiatives from problem definition through implementation. Establish technical requirements, milestones, dependencies, success measures, and accountability across Engineering, Product, Quality, Regulatory, and Operations.
Build Automation and Internal Tooling: Design, prototype, implement, and maintain scripts, integrations, dashboards, and workflow applications using Oracle APEX, Python, SQL, APIs, or comparable technologies. Streamline intake, approvals, reporting, and program execution.
Apply Codex and AI-Assisted Development: Use Codex and related tools to accelerate automation development, prototyping, testing, and documentation. Review and test generated outputs, applying appropriate controls when tooling supports regulated processes.
Connect Automation With Medical Device Compliance: Partner with Quality and Regulatory Affairs to identify opportunities to automate requirements tracking, traceability, evidence collection, change tracking, and readiness reporting. Ensure solutions support applicable documentation, review, and validation requirements.
Drive Medical Device Regulatory Readiness: Lead integrated plans supporting medical device certification, regulatory reviews, audits, and international expansion. Translate regulatory and quality requirements into actionable engineering and operational deliverables with clear ownership.
Strengthen Technical Documentation: Coordinate Engineering and Product teams to produce complete, consistent, and traceable documentation supporting development, verification and validation, risk management, and product launches.
Lead Release Readiness: Drive end-to-end release coordination, including engineering dependencies, quality and regulatory deliverables, readiness criteria, risk resolution, and stakeholder communication.
Partner With Operations Leadership: Serve as a strategic thought partner to the Director of Operations. Support OP1/OP2 planning, headcount and capacity planning, investment prioritization, and execution of organization-wide initiatives.
Turn Data Into Decisions: Build reliable reporting and analyze engineering, operational, and workforce data to identify bottlenecks, flag risks, and recommend actions. Measure improvements in cycle time, manual effort, delivery predictability, and compliance readiness.
Influence Across the Organization: Lead executive discussions, communicate technical tradeoffs clearly, and drive decisions across teams. Establish reusable tools and practices, mentor partners, and build trust while maintaining accountability.

Experience translating regulatory and quality requirements into technical plans, operational workflows, and documented evidence.

Demonstrated experience partnering with VP- and Director-level leaders on planning, prioritization, and execution.

Executive presence, clear communication, and emotional intelligence, with the ability to lead discussions across Engineering, Product, Legal, Regulatory, Quality, and Finance.

Experience automating documentation, traceability, or evidence workflows within a regulated medical device environment.

new_jobs.description:
Role: Finance Program Manager – Quote to Cash
Location: San Jose, CA

Duration: 6 Months

The Opportunity

Client is seeking a high-impact Finance Program Manager to drive our Quote to Cash (Q2C) transformation , spanning deal structuring and pricing, order management, billing, revenue recognition, and collections. This role sits at the intersection of delivery leadership and operational excellence, with the opportunity to help redesign the processes and systems that power how Client quotes, contracts, invoices, and collects from customers at scale.
The ideal candidate is ready to own end-to-end Q2C transformation as an operator invested in the outcome, with fluency across the finance, sales operations, deal desk, legal, and IT stakeholders who touch the quote-to-cash lifecycle. They can move fluidly from process redesign to detailed operational planning. They structure executive-level recommendations and hold cross-functional teams accountable for delivery.
This program manager will help build a "transformation muscle" within Finance by regularly recognizing, applying, and documenting standard methodologies and controls that guide Client’s Quote to Cash playbook.

What You’ll Do:

Own the delivery of Quote to Cash transformation initiative planning and design, including scope definition across pricing/CPQ, order management, billing, revenue recognition, and collections workstreams, deliverables tracking, and definition and measurement of success criteria (e.g., quote cycle time, billing accuracy, DSO).
Drive rigorous cross-functional execution and program delivery across Sales Operations, Deal Desk, Legal, Revenue Accounting, Treasury, and IT, ensuring accountability across teams while supporting and maintaining established Q2C governance frameworks and controls.
Influence and guide key business partners: Lead through influence with Sales, Legal, Revenue Accounting, and IT teams outside your direct reporting line. Act as a credible thought partner to senior executives, effectively representing Q2C transformation priorities and trade-offs.
Support program resource planning, budget, and resource management; manage third-party vendors and system-integrator partners delivering CPQ, billing, and revenue recognition system enhancements
Enable organizational learning and capability building through identification and codification of Q2C process patterns, frameworks, and best practices across quoting, contracting, billing, and cash application
Help design the future-state Quote to Cash operating model for Finance that will serve as an operational mechanism to drive transformation across Finance and its cross-functional stakeholders

EXPERIENCE:

Program/Portfolio Manager or Project Lead-equivalent experience; alternatively, 6-8+ years in a high-impact internal Quote to Cash, finance transformation, or revenue operations role at a leading global company.
Demonstrated track record of leading complex, multi-stakeholder transformations from problem definition through implementation – with clear accountability for business outcomes
Strong communication and people management skills, with the ability to drive impact through influence and to lead senior leaders through defined narratives/storyboards
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including translating data into actionable insights.
Exposure to enterprise-scale Quote to Cash systems and processes – including CPQ, contract management, billing, revenue recognition (ASC 606), and collections platforms (e.g., Client, SAP, Zuora, or equivalent). Background in enterprise SaaS, technology, or digital transformation environments preferred.
Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Operations Management, or a related area; equivalent experience will also be taken into account
